newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Citicorp's Brazil unit says launches Visa cards.
newsitem.headline: Citicorp's Brazil unit says launches Visa cards.

text.p: Citicorp unit Citibank, Brazil will begin to offer Visa credit cards beginning September, a bank executive said.
The launch of Citibank Visa credit cards is part of the bank's strategy to expand its number of clients, said Rodrigo de Britto, executive director for credit cards at Citibank, Brazil.
"Everywhere the credit card is the bank's main door to the client," he told a news conference.
The Brazilian unit of Citicorp has currently 94,000 banking clients, of which 80 percent own a credit card. It aims to have 250,000 clients by the year 2000.
Citibank Brazil was the only Citicorp's unit in the world which had not offered Visa credit cards, Britto said.

Citibank, which manages over 50 million credits cards in the world, has approximately 100,000 Credicard/Mastercard credit card accounts in Brazil. With the Visa credit cards, the bank plans to reach year's end with 100,000 more cards and one million credit cards by the year 2000.
The Visa credit cards will be administered by Credicard, of which Citibank is a major shareholder, Britto added.
